segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Taking it fully offline wasn't realistic — that's our only remote-access path for twelve hundred people, including trading desk staff.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A substantive continuity and availability constraint supporting the decision, without a hidden bias mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: We have six years of ACLs and firewall rules tuned exactly to how our network behaves — I know that system cold. Honestly, I didn't sit down and actually work through what a fast-tracked migration's rollback plan or transition controls would have looked like on that timeline; I just gave staying extra weight because it was the environment I already knew inside and out.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly gives the familiar existing system extra weight and does not comparatively evaluate the migration alternative, matching Status Quo Bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: That breach a peer firm had a couple years back ... was very much in my head when I was explaining to leadership why we needed to move fast on the patch specifically. ... I used that story more than the actual advisory language when I was framing the urgency internally.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A vivid recalled peer ransomware incident was given more weight than the current advisory when communicating risk, matching Availability Bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, that 98% figure just read better. '98% success' sounds a lot more solid than '2% incident rate,' even though — yeah, in hindsight those are the same number. At the time I didn't sit down and do that conversion.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant preferred statistically equivalent information because of its positive versus negative wording, matching Framing Bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Five out of six firms choosing the same platform felt like a strong signal on its own. I didn't push hard on whether any of them had our specific legacy app footprint ... I figured if that many peers were comfortable, the risk was manageable.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Peer-adoption volume substituted for independent compatibility verification, matching the Bandwagon effect.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: We were down a person — my other engineer was out — and the vendor's two-week default felt like it assumed more hands than we had.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A genuine staffing-based operational rationale; the hidden Overconfidence instance is mapped to the separate generalization from prior cutovers.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I've done three cutovers before without any formal parallel-run phase at all and they went fine, so a compressed one-week window with the new platform felt reasonable ... those earlier cutovers were on architecture I already knew well. This was a genuinely different authentication model, and I didn't really weigh that difference.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant generalized from prior successes to a materially different architecture and compressed a recommended safety margin, matching Overconfidence Bias.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The candidate is a speculative confirmation-bias interpretation of the peer outreach, while the hidden instance is Bandwagon effect. The transcript does not establish that the outreach was selected to confirm an already-formed choice or that disconfirming evidence was available and ignored.

candidates.details: The candidate is clearly hedged and explains why it was not promoted to an identified finding. It is useful as a diagnostic possibility, but remains a false positive when the candidate tier is scored because the hidden target ontology contains no Confirmation bias instance and the evidence is insufficient for that construct.

high_only.detection_interpretation: High-confidence findings detect the status-quo and framing segments, with no false alarms, but miss the three moderate/low-confidence target segments.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: Including moderate-confidence findings recovers the bandwagon and overconfidence segments while still missing only the low-confidence availability segment.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: All five hidden positive segments are detected by identified findings, with both negative segments correctly rejected and no segment-level false alarms.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: The candidate adds no segment-level coverage because it is localized to an already detected positive segment; segment metrics therefore remain unchanged.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: The candidate concerns possibly favoring supportive peer evidence, while the hidden target concerns substituting majority adoption for independent compatibility verification.
primary_error_types: candidate false positive at fourth threshold

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG output explicitly states that no retrieved corpus passages were used and supplies no citation metadata. Corpus fidelity is therefore unavailable, but no unsupported retrieval claim or citation inconsistency is present.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Recall rises from 0.4000 to 0.8000 and F1 from 0.5714 to 0.8889, with no false-alarm increase.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: Recall and F1 both rise to 1.0000 by adding the low-confidence Availability finding, with no false-alarm increase.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: Segment metrics remain unchanged; instance precision falls to 0.8333 and F1 to 0.9091 because the Confirmation bias candidate is an extra false positive.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, 4 of 5 positive segments were detected, all 2 negative segments were correctly rejected, and there were no segment-level false alarms.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: All five hidden instances are correctly labeled or matched by an approved equivalent, localized, and supported by the required mechanism when all identified confidence levels are included; high_and_moderate captures 4 of 5.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Mechanism-first and strict results are identical: every identified finding has both an equivalent target label and a full mechanism match, so there is no taxonomy gap.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The single Confirmation bias candidate is a useful cautious abstention diagnostically, but it is a false positive when candidates are counted because the evidence is insufficient and the construct is not a hidden target.
main_failure_modes: Three correct findings were below the high-confidence threshold, reducing high-only recall.
The candidate tier introduces one instance-level false positive without improving segment coverage.
main_strengths: All five hidden instances are correctly localized and mechanism-matched at the all-identified threshold.
No identified finding is unsupported, duplicated, fabricated, or assigned to a negative segment.
The output appropriately distinguishes the low-confidence Availability finding and the speculative Confirmation bias candidate.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong evidence-grounded detection with a confidence-calibration tradeoff: high-only is precise but underdetects, the recommended high_and_moderate threshold recovers four targets without false alarms, and all identified findings recover the complete hidden manifest. Candidate scoring adds diagnostic breadth but lowers instance precision because the extra candidate is not a target match.
